chunks: Al-Shaykh al-Faqih Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Wahb al-Basri narrated to us. He said: Thawaba ibn Mas'ud narrated to me, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

A son of Uthman ibn Maz'un (may Allah be pleased with him) passed away, and his grief intensified to the point where he took a place in his house as a place of worship to devote himself in prayer therein. This reached the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family), and he said to him: O Uthman, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has not prescribed monasticism for us. The monasticism of my nation is striving in the way of Allah.

O Uthman ibn Maz'un, Paradise has eight gates and the Hellfire has seven gates. Would it not gladden you that you will not approach any gate of them except that you find your son at your side, holding onto your waistband, interceding for you to your Lord? He said: Indeed, yes. So the Muslims said: And for us too, O Messenger of Allah, regarding our departed children, is there what Uthman has? He said: Yes, for whoever among you is patient and seeks reward from Allah.

Then he said: O Uthman, whoever prays the Fajr prayer in congregation, then sits remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until the sun rises, shall have seventy ranks in the Highest Paradise, the distance between every two ranks being like the gallop of a swift, lean horse for seventy years. And whoever prays Dhuhr in congregation shall have fifty ranks in the Gardens of Eden, the distance between every two ranks being like the gallop of a swift horse for fifty years. And whoever prays Asr in congregation shall have the reward of freeing eight descendants of Isma'il, each of them being the head of a household. And whoever prays Maghrib in congregation shall have the reward of a virtuous Hajj and an accepted Umra. And whoever prays Isha in congregation shall have the reward of keeping vigil on the Night of Power.

key_terms.جهاد: Striving (jihad) - the Islamic alternative to monasticism
key_terms.رهبانية: Monasticism (rahbaniyyah) - withdrawal from worldly life for worship, explicitly rejected for Muslims
key_terms.شفاعة: Intercession (shafa'ah) - deceased children pleading for their parents at Paradise gates
key_terms.ليلة القدر: Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) - the equivalent reward for congregational Isha prayer

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about monasticism and the reward of congregational prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq narrates how the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) consoled Uthman ibn Maz'un after the death of his son. The Prophet first rejected the concept of monasticism in Islam, declaring that the monasticism of his nation is jihad (striving) in the way of Allah. He then comforted Uthman with the teaching that children who die before their parents will intercede for them at the eight gates of Paradise. The Prophet concluded by enumerating the immense spiritual rewards for each of the five daily congregational prayers, from seventy degrees in the highest Paradise for Fajr to a reward equivalent to standing on the Night of Power for Isha.
